messages:
ops-bot: SLO BURN ALERT: hosted-api.gateway - 5xx rate spiked to 4.7% (SLO 0.5%) over the last 10m. Alert ID: AB-9072. Sample traces low.

olivia (oncall): seeing it, thanks. Is this global or a single region?

ops-bot: Regions affected: us-west-2, eu-west-1. Error mix: 502 gateway + net timeouts.

kevin (support): multiple customers just opened tickets — they report timeouts ~25-30s and then a 502. One customer included a curl repro: `curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"model":"xlarge","input":"hi"}'` -> hangs then 502.

olivia (oncall): tagging eng-runtime. @angelo can you take? I'll start basic triage.

angelo (eng-runtime): on it. first check: scaling and recent deploys. @release-bot any deploys in the last hour to hosted-api?

release-bot: Recent rollouts: hosted-api: v2026.03.15-rc3 -> started 1769994100, completed 1769994205. Canary 10% -> promoting to 100% at 1769994250. No rollback.

angelo (eng-runtime): that timing lines up with the burn. Can we confirm whether the 502s correlate with deploy window?

ingrid (observability): pulling logs. Query I'm running: 
```
index=prod logs service=hosted-api.gateway status>=500 | stats count() by status, region
```
Prelim shows a spike of 502s starting ~1769994230 in us-west-2 and eu-west-1.

taj (eng-sre): any trace ids? ops-bot said sample traces low. Might be proxy-level timeouts so traces from downstream don't show up.

kevin (support): customer provided a response header snapshot: `x-proxy: envoy`, `x-envoy-upstream-service-time: N/A`, `via: 1.1 gateway`. They also included raw body: "Gateway Timeout".

olivia (oncall): hypothesis: proxy (envoy) timeouts or upstream model worker stall under the canary change. Two parallel mitigations: 1) increase proxy timeout temporarily (to prevent 502s from being returned immediately) and 2) route traffic off the canary (rollback or pause promotion).

angelo (eng-runtime): I can pause promotion and route 100% back to v2026.03.14. Initiating traffic shift. Running command: 
```
# switch traffic back to stable
kubectl -n hosted scale deployment hosted-api-canary --replicas=0
kubectl -n hosted patch svc hosted-api --patch '{"spec":{"selector":{"version":"stable"}}}'
```

olivia (oncall): while you're doing that I'll bump envoy proxy timeout from 20s -> 60s in the LB config as short-term. @ingrid, make sure we capture proxy metrics.

ingrid (observability): adding dashboard panel: envoys.request_time_p95 by region and envoy. Also running a span-sampling query to look for dropped spans: 
```
service:hosted-api.gateway | where status >= 500 | fields trace_id, span_count, sample_rate
```
Result: most 502s have trace_id=null or span_count=0 => probes not reaching instrumented code. Suggests proxy timeouts or connection resets.

angelo (eng-runtime): traffic switch done. Rolling back canary promoted tasks marked draining. Confirming endpoints now point to stable.

ops-bot: Alert: 5xx rate dropping to 1.8% after rollback and timeout bump. Still above SLO but trending down.

kevin (support): customers reporting immediate improvement. One customer said latency returned to normal and retries succeeded.

taj (eng-sre): check worker/backplane health (model servers, redis, k8s node CPU). Running quick node health query: 
```
kubectl top pods -n hosted | grep model
```
No OOMs, CPU looks normal. Per-host TCP stats show increased SYN retries on proxy nodes around 1769994235.

ingrid (observability): I suspect ephemeral connection exhaustion on edge proxies. Traces absent because connections fail before app-level instrumentation. I'm running a netstat/conntrack check on proxy host: 
```
sudo ss -s; ss -tn state syn-recv
```
conntrack shows high count of TIME_WAIT on envoy nodes, and ephemeral port usage nearing limit on two nodes in us-west-2.

angelo (eng-runtime): that explains it — when ports exhausted envoy returns 502 quickly. What changed in canary to increase conn churn? New connection-handling code in v2026.03.15 that disables keepalive? Checking diffs now.

angelo (eng-runtime): found it. Canary included a libc upgrade that altered keepalive defaults in the worker runtime (shorter keepalive, more connections). Reproducer in PR: https://git.redwood.ai/p/runtime/PR-3345

olivia (oncall): good catch. We should keep rollback and then revert that libc bump. For immediate mitigation, increase ephemeral port range and decrease TIME_WAIT TTL on proxies, and add connection pool tuning.

angelo (eng-runtime): opened rollback ticket and revert PR now. Patch submitted: revert libc bump from canary. Also adding quick proxy sysctl change: 
```
# increase ephemeral ports and decrease TIME_WAIT
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range=\"15000 61000\"
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30
```

ingrid (observability): dashboard panels updated: envoys.conn_count, TIME_WAIT, p95 upstream response time. Will add an alert for ephemeral port usage at 85% to avoid future silent failures.

kevin (support): created a customer-facing summary for affected tickets: short explain "transient gateway timeouts caused by new runtime change increasing connection churn; we've reverted canary and increased proxy timeouts; monitoring in place; please reopen if you still see errors."

ops-bot: Incident state: mitigation in place. 5xx back to 0.35% (under SLO). Ticket AB-9072 -> incident-176999.

olivia (oncall): postmortem owners: taj (eng-sre) + angelo (eng-runtime) + ingrid (observability). Please write a short incident report in the incidents channel and link to this thread. Action items: 
- revert PR confirmed and validated on prod (angelo)
- add ephemeral-port alert (ingrid)
- add a canary checklist item to validate connection metrics (taj)
- create runbook step for increasing proxy timeouts for quick mitigation (olivia)

taj (eng-sre): will create a follow-up JIRA for the canary checklist and add the netstat check to our CI canary smoke tests.

angelo (eng-runtime): revert deployed, proxy sysctl patched on affected nodes, scaling and traffic healthy. I'll follow up in incidents with the change diff and the rollback diff.

kevin (support): I'll send the customer notices now. Tagging docs for a short blurb if needed.

olivia (oncall): closing loop — we'll monitor for one hour, then close incident. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Note: create postmortem within 72h or auto-escalate.

olivia (oncall): noted. I'll start the draft.
